title: Statistics & Probability for Beginners: A Complete Step-by-Step Self-Study Course and Work
description: Statistics & Probability for Beginners turns difficult ideas into clear, manageable steps. Designed for high-school and college students, independent learners, and anyone beginning data-focused study, this guide combines explanation with meaningful practice. Inside you will find: • Beginner-friendly lessons • Step-by-step worked examples • “Try It” questions for immediate practice • Exercises with complete answers and explanations • Tables, graphs, visual guides, and formula summaries • Probability rules, distributions, sampling, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, ANOVA, correlation, and regression • Real-world examples that develop statistical judgment • Comprehensive review and critical-value tables Learn to select the right method, calculate accurately, interpret results in context, and recognize misleading statistical claims. title: The Art of Statistics: How to Learn from Data
description: In this "important and comprehensive" (New Yorker) guide to statistical thinking, discover how you can use data and mathematics to gain a better understanding of life’s biggest problems. The age of big data has made statistical literacy more important than ever. In The Art of Statistics , David Spiegelhalter shows how to apply statistical reasoning to real-world problems. Whether we're analyzing preventative medical screening or the terrible crime sprees of serial killers, Spiegelhalter teaches us how to clarify questions, assumptions, and expectations and, most importantly, how to interpret the answers we receive. title: Statistics for Absolute Beginners (Second Edition) (Learn Statistics & Probability Books f
description: Most statistics textbooks are designed for mathematicians. This one is designed for you. Written in plain English and illustrated throughout to support visual learners, this book removes the fear and confusion from learning statistics. Each chapter is carefully structured to break down complex concepts and build knowledge without boring or losing you along the way. This includes revisiting the same datasets across multiple chapters, so you don't have to spend time learning a new dataset to grasp each new technique. Everything builds on what came before, and by Chapter 15, you won't just understand statistics, you'll know how to run probabilistic analysis and Z-tests using your own data. What makes this book different Most beginner stats books lead with complex formulas and follow with dry, textbook examples. This book does the opposite. The story comes first, and the methods emerge naturally from it. From a dentist who faked a marathon to a golfer who crossed Mongolia with a single iron club, the case studies are genuinely interesting stories that happen to teach statistics, helping you remember each method because you remember the story. What you’ll learn: Learn the essentials of probabilistic prediction with real-life examples, from gambling in 16th-Century Italy to calculating the likelihood of your friends showing up to dinner. Design and conduct Z-Tests and T-Tests with confidence, using step-by-step worked examples you can immediately apply to your own data. Build and interpret linear regression models and Pearson correlation to uncover relationships hidden in your data. Master the essentials of hypothesis testing and learn to distinguish what is statistically meaningful from what happened purely by chance. Discover clustering analysis techniques used daily in mac

title: Bayesian Statistics the Fun Way: Understanding Statistics and Probability with Star Wars,
description: Fun guide to learning Bayesian statistics and probability through unusual and illustrative examples. Probability and statistics are increasingly important in a huge range of professions. But many people use data in ways they don't even understand, meaning they aren't getting the most from it. Bayesian Statistics the Fun Way will change that. This book will give you a complete understanding of Bayesian statistics through simple explanations and un-boring examples. Find out the probability of UFOs landing in your garden, how likely Han Solo is to survive a flight through an asteroid shower, how to win an argument about conspiracy theories, and whether a burglary really was a burglary, to name a few examples. By using these off-the-beaten-track examples, the author actually makes learning statistics fun. And you'll learn real skills, like how to: - How to measure your own level of uncertainty in a conclusion or belief - Calculate Bayes theorem and understand what it's useful for - Find the posterior, likelihood, and prior to check the accuracy of your conclusions - Calculate distributions to see the range of your data - Compare hypotheses and draw reliable conclusions from them Next time you find yourself with a sheaf of survey results and no idea what to do with them, turn to Bayesian Statistics the Fun Way to get the most value from your data.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_0"]', '#CardInstancex0Zn2GxNoCJgHOS7NRsEnA')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_0',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-block;-webkit-filter:none;filter:none;-webkit-filter:var(--aok-sf

title: Probability Fundamentals: An Intuitive Guide to Understanding Uncertainty
description: Gain a decision-making edge by learning probability in a way that actually makes sense! Probability affects far more of our lives than most people realize. It shapes medical testing, risk assessment, scientific research, and decision-making. Yet it is an area where intuition breaks down easily. Build the skills to reason clearly under uncertainty, solve real-world problems, and avoid the intuitive mistakes that lead people astray. Probability Fundamentals helps you develop a practical understanding using clear explanations and real-world applications. Understand the reasoning behind the calculations so they don’t feel mysterious. Along the way, you’ll solve counterintuitive problems that make probability both fascinating and challenging. Learn the fundamentals of probability and uncertainty: Learn how to apply probabilistic thinking. Use contingency tables and empirical probabilities to analyze data. Learn and apply the core probability rules correctly. Interpret conditional probabilities, independence, and risk. Use Bayes’ Theorem and Bayesian thinking to update probabilities. Learn counting methods and combinatorics. Work with the binomial, normal, Poisson, and related distributions. Calculate probabilities, confidence intervals, and p-values. Build practical skills with 100+ practice problems. title: Essential Mathematics, Statistics and Probability for AI & Machine Learning: A Practical G
description: The mathematics that machine learning is actually built from and nothing else You do not need a degree in mathematics to build useful machine learning systems, but you do need to speak the language . A neural network multiplies matrices and adds biases . A loss function subtracts a prediction from a target and squares the result. A classifier outputs a probability , and you decide what to do with it. A data pipeline computes ratios , percentages and averages long before the model ever sees a row. This book supplies exactly that mathematics: the 25 chapters, in the order you need them is roughly 1k pages, written for people who want to stop treating machine learning as a black box. What makes this book different Relevance above completeness. A topic earns its place only if some machine learning method depends on it. One good example. Each idea is shown once, carefully, and then the book moves on with a running example. Plain words first, notation second. Every concept is explained in ordinary language before the symbols arrive, so gradient , Bayes' theorem stop being words you nod along to. Real mathematics, properly typeset. Every formula is rendered as real mathematics , show as in a lecture hall. No chapter is code-first. Short, readable Python snippets appear only where they make an idea concrete. Four parts, one continuous path Part I — Mathematical Foundations. The grammar of the subject: numbers, arithmetic and algebra ; functions, graphs and notation ; vectors ; matrices ; linear transformations ; derivatives and the chain rule ; and optimization and gradient descent .
